incident.report: Auction success rate dropped sharply shortly after the auction backend was deployed this afternoon. Identify the likely cause, show the supporting evidence, and test a remediation without touching the live system.

alert.definition: share of publisher auction requests answered 201 with status COMPLETED within 2s

hypotheses.statement: Deploy 1.3.0 shrank the backend connection pool to 2+0. Auctions queue for a connection and miss the publishers' 2 s timeout while Postgres sits idle.
A schema change made a hot query slow.
A setting changed in the same deploy caused the drop.

timeline.event: success rate drops below half of its baseline

result.finding: publishers hit their 2s timeout and auction duration_ms climbs into seconds, yet DSP bids stay VALID at their usual 25-70ms response times, ruling out slow bidders
backend logs show SQLAlchemy QueuePool limit/timeout errors starting right after the deploy
pg_stat_activity samples fall from ~20 connections to a handful, mostly 'idle in transaction', with no lock waits, so Postgres itself is idle rather than overloaded
the deploy's config diff shrinks DB_POOL_SIZE and DB_MAX_OVERFLOW

fixed_workflow.rationale: Restore DB_POOL_SIZE=20 and DB_MAX_OVERFLOW=10 (or size the pool above rps x hold time).

agent_offline.rationale: Restore DB_POOL_SIZE=20 and DB_MAX_OVERFLOW=10 (or size the pool above rps x hold time).

ground_truth.summary: Deploy v1.3.0 cut the backend's connection pool from 20+10 to 2+0. Each auction holds a connection for roughly the whole ~100ms DSP fan-out, so the pool now serves about 14 auctions/s against 24/s of traffic. Requests queue for a connection, latency climbs past the publishers' 2s timeout, and success collapses even though Postgres itself is idle.
distinguishing_evidence: publishers hit their 2s timeout and auction duration_ms climbs into seconds, yet DSP bids stay VALID at their usual 25-70ms response times, ruling out slow bidders
backend logs show SQLAlchemy QueuePool limit/timeout errors starting right after the deploy
pg_stat_activity samples fall from ~20 connections to a handful, mostly 'idle in transaction', with no lock waits, so Postgres itself is idle rather than overloaded
the deploy's config diff shrinks DB_POOL_SIZE and DB_MAX_OVERFLOW

remediation.description: Restore DB_POOL_SIZE=20 and DB_MAX_OVERFLOW=10 (or size the pool above rps x hold time).

ground_truth.summary: Release 1.5.0 ran migration 0004, which rebuilt auction.request_id and dropped its UNIQUE constraint, and with it the only index on the column. Every auction starts with an idempotency lookup by request_id, which is now a sequential scan over two million rows. Each request holds a pooled connection for the scan, the pool queues, and requests miss their 2s timeout while DSPs stay fast.
distinguishing_evidence: active queries show the SELECT on auction by request_id running for hundreds of ms
sequential scans on auction jump from ~0 to one or more per request, with millions of tuples read
DSP response times are unchanged, ruling out slow bidders

remediation.description: Roll back migration 0004 (re-create the unique index on auction.request_id).

ground_truth.component: auction-events topic / worker consumers (message that fails deserialization)
ground_truth.summary: A truncated JSON message landed on auction-events. The worker's consumers decode messages in the Kafka client's deserializer, outside the retry and dead-letter path, so the exception kills the whole worker process. It restarts, reads the same uncommitted message, and dies again. Auctions still succeed, but nothing downstream is consumed: consumer lag grows and the analytics rollup falls further behind every second.
distinguishing_evidence: worker logs show repeated JSONDecodeError tracebacks and worker_starting lines
consumer lag grows on all three groups while their committed offsets stay put

remediation.description: Skip the one undecodable message (advance the stuck groups' offsets by one).

fixed_workflow.rationale: the investigation abstained; rolling back the suspect deploy's risky settings shows whether that deploy alone explains the drop

agent_offline.rationale: the investigation abstained; rolling back the suspect deploy's risky settings shows whether that deploy alone explains the drop

ground_truth.component: backend setting AUCTION_GLOBAL_TIMEOUT_MS together with slower DSP-A, DSP-B, DSP-D, DSP-E
ground_truth.summary: Neither change alone breaks auctions: the bidders at ~85ms fit in the old 100ms deadline, and the 80ms deadline is fine for bidders at 25-60ms. Together, every call to the four slowed bidders is cut at 80ms. The telemetry cannot tell this apart from "the bidders became too slow for any deadline", because their real latency is never observed: every call ends at the 80ms cut. Abstaining, or ranking both causes, is the honest answer; a sandbox experiment that restores the 100ms deadline settles it (success recovers).
distinguishing_evidence: TIMEOUT bids for DSP-A/B/D/E land at ~80ms, the new global deadline, so their true latency is censored
DSP-A answered in ~26ms before the deploy and now times out at 80ms, so the bidders did slow down
the deploy lowered AUCTION_GLOBAL_TIMEOUT_MS from 100 to 80 at the same moment

remediation.description: Roll AUCTION_GLOBAL_TIMEOUT_MS back to 100. Raising per-DSP timeouts alone does not help, since the 80ms global deadline still cuts every call.
